result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.find_isomorphism()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a node correspondence that shows two graphs are isomorphic. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17593-L17672){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.find_isomorphism( other, node_attr=None, edge_attr=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Find isomorphism](/assets/graphs/find-isomorphism.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two directed graphs drawn differently. Graph a is a workflow where fetch points to build and test, and build points to test; graph b has nodes s1, s2, s3 with s1 pointing to s2 and s3, and s2 pointing to s3. Matching colors pair each node of a with its partner in b, and the card returns the mapping fetch to s1 (accent), build to s2 (teal), and test to s3 (violet), under which every edge of a lands on an edge of b." width="100%"} Where `is_isomorphic()` answers yes or no, this method returns the correspondence itself: a dictionary that maps every node of this graph to its partner in `other`, so that two nodes are joined in this graph exactly when their partners are joined in `other`. It is the tool for aligning two versions of the same network whose labels differ, such as matching atoms between two drawings of a molecule or nodes between two exports of the same system. When several correspondences exist (for example in a symmetric graph), one of them is returned. Use `subgraph_isomorphisms()` with `other` as the pattern to list them all. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `Graph` to compare with. It is not modified. [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute name, or list of names, whose values must be equal for matched nodes. [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute name, or list of names, whose values must be equal for matched edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int] or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A mapping from node IDs of this graph to node IDs of `other`, or `None` if the graphs are not isomorphic. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Uses the same search as `is_isomorphic()` (color refinement followed by a VF2++ style backtracking search) and stops at the first complete correspondence. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The same three-step workflow, exported twice with different names: ::: {#68033511 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec a = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["fetch", "build", "test"]) a.add_edges([("fetch", "build"), ("build", "test"), ("fetch", "test")]) b = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["s1", "s2", "s3"]) b.add_edges([("s2", "s3"), ("s1", "s3"), ("s1", "s2")]) mapping = a.find_isomorphism(b) {a.get_label_from_id(k): b.get_label_from_id(v) for k, v in mapping.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'fetch': 's1', 'build': 's2', 'test': 's3'} ``` ::: ::: Graphs with different structure have no correspondence: ::: {#bf52308a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} a.find_isomorphism(ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(3)) is None ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
